identity.title: ALMA observations of anisotropic dust mass loss in the inner circumstellar environment of the red supergiant VY Canis Majoris

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this Letter we report the results of a sub-100 mas study of this region using ALMA Science Verification data.

evidence.quote: Using a distance of 1.2 kpc to VY CMa, this angular distance corresponds to 400 AU

distance_source.value: not stated (relative proximity cited to Zhang et al. 2012)

evidence.quote: Using a distance of 1.2 kpc to VY CMa, this angular distance corresponds to 400 AU

question.value: What are the properties and distribution of dust in the inner circumstellar envelope of the red supergiant VY CMa, and what does it imply for mass-loss mechanisms?

evidence.quote: In this Letter we report the results of a sub-100 mas study of this region using ALMA Science Verification data.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00011.SV.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 321 GHz, 325 GHz, 658 GHz observed; 1.74 GHz line-free continuum at 321 GHz and 0.4 GHz at 658 GHz used

evidence.quote: we used a total of $1.74$ GHz line free continuum channels around 321 GHz and $0.4$ GHz centered on 658 GHz.
using 16 to 20 antennas of the main array with projected baselines ranging from 14 m to 2.7 km
as part of the ALMA Science Verification process on 2013 16-19 August

provided.value: F1042M image from 1999 March 22 for comparison

evidence.quote: an *HST*/WFPC2 exposure of VY CMa taken with the F1042M filter on 1999 March 22

what.value: Single-dish and SMA (sub-)mm flux density compilations

evidence.quote: using the compilations of (cite: knapp_1993) and (cite: ladjal_2010)

external_data_from_literature.citation: Knapp et al. 1993; Ladjal et al. 2010; Shinnaga 2004; Muller 2007; Kaminski 2013

what.value: Stellar radius 1420 Rsun and Teff 3490 K

evidence.quote: we have assumed a stellar radius of $R_{\star}= 1420\,R_{\odot}$ (6.84 AU or 5.7 mas) and an effective temperature $T_{\mathrm{eff}}= 3490\,$K (cite: wittkowski_2012)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Harper et al. (2001) semi-empirical Betelgeuse atmosphere model scaled to VY CMa for stellar contribution

evidence.quote: we scaled the (cite: harper_2001) semi-empirical model for the M2 Iab RSG Betelgeuse (without the silicate dust) to the angular diameter of VY CMa.
based on the $\pm 15\%$ uncertainty of the absolute flux calibration (R+14)

smoothing.value: 658 GHz data convolved with 321 GHz synthesized beam and regridded for spectral index map

evidence.quote: after convolving the 658 GHz data with the synthesized beam from the 321 GHz image, and regridding the convolved image to match the pixel scale
Details of the observations and data processing are provided in (cite: richards_2014), hereafter R+14.

unstated_but_needed: CASA version, calibration and imaging parameters (weighting, robust, cell, clean settings)
Phase offset corrections beyond the quoted shift, and the beam sizes (in table not provided in the text)
Dust temperature structure and masking used for the resolved-out flux estimate

method.value: 2-D cross-correlation over range of shifts; maximum correlation gives offset

evidence.quote: we shifted the 658 GHz image relative the 321 GHz image and computed a 2-D cross-correlation function for a range of shifts.

validation.value: Similar to correction found by R+14

evidence.quote: similar to the correction found by R+14 when aligning the peak position of the second brightest continuum component

method.value: 2-D elliptical Gaussian fits, deconvolved sizes and fluxes

evidence.quote: We fit 2-D elliptical Gaussian components to the two main continuum features

method.value: Ratio of beam-matched 658 and 321 GHz images, pixels above 6 sigma

evidence.quote: All data below the $6\sigma _{\mathrm{rms}}$ noise level in the convolved 658 GHz image have been omitted

method.value: Optically thin Rayleigh-Jeans dust mass equation with stellar contribution subtracted; temperature from radiative heating

evidence.quote: Equation [\[eq1\]](#eq1) can be re-arranged to find the total mass of dust in each of the two main continuum components.

assumptions.value: a_g = 0.2 micron, rho_g = 3.5 g cm^-3, Q = 5.65e-4 (nu/274.6 GHz)^0.7, Tstar = 3490 K

method.value: Estimate resolved-out flux vs single-dish, dust mass over 8 arcsec shell at 200 K, divided by timescale

evidence.quote: We assume the dust to be extended over the $\sim8\ensuremath{''}$ size of the *HST* image
We assume an average temperature of 200 K throughout the shell.
The middle region of the main continuum component C has a spectral index of $\alpha \sim 1.9$
has a spectral index of $\alpha \sim 2.7$

results_numeric.quantity: Dust mass of C at 321 GHz

evidence.quote: We then derive dust masses of $2.5\times 10^{-4}\,M_{\odot}$ at 321 GHz
a dust mass-loss rate of $5\times10^{-6}(V_{\rm{d}}/60~$km s$^{-1})\,$M$_{\odot}\,$yr$^{-1}$
is 334 mas SE of the star in the plane of the sky

findings_qualitative.value: Brightest continuum component C is offset from the star and is possibly optically thick/cool; thermal molecular emission avoids it

evidence.quote: we find that the thermal molecular emission lines from the ALMA data avoids the C component

claims.hypothesis: Is dust mass loss from VY CMa isotropic?
claims.experiment: Sub-100 mas ALMA continuum imaging at 321 and 658 GHz
claims.result: Two resolved components and N-NE extension; C is 400 AU SE of star
claims.finding: Dust mass loss is anisotropic with clumps; >17% of dust is in clumps

evidence.quote: We can thus conclude that $>17\%$ of the dust mass around VY CMa is located in clumps

claims.hypothesis: Is convection alone driving the mass loss?
claims.experiment: Compare the persistent directed clumps with expectations
claims.result: Continuous directed dust loss over 30-50 yr
claims.finding: A localized, stable (possibly magnetic) mechanism is needed

evidence.quote: A mass-loss mechanism that is localized but much more stable over time (i.e., over a few decades) is required to explain our observations.

limitations_admitted.value: Dust mass of C is a lower limit as it may not be optically thin; much flux is resolved out

evidence.quote: The main component C may not be fully optically thin at both frequencies and so its dust mass estimates will be lower limits.

referee_caveats_inferred: Dust mass depends on assumed emissivity law and grain properties
Resolved-out flux estimate assumes same spectral index at all scales

missing_for_reproduction: Beam and rms values (tables not in text)
reproducibility.score_reason: Public SV data and simple analysis, but processing is deferred to R+14 and imaging settings are absent.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Processing details are inherited from R+14 and not given here.
